metadata.note: SPGI is a credit rating agency and financial data provider. Prediction markets on credit ratings, recession, inflation, and interest rates are directly relevant to SPGI's business environment and revenue drivers.

macro_events.spgi_relevance: Recession reduces debt issuance volume (SPGI Ratings revenue) but increases demand for risk analytics (S&P Global Market Intelligence). Net effect historically negative for SPGI revenue growth.
Negative GDP directly correlates with reduced corporate capital market activity, impacting SPGI Ratings issuance fees.
Persistent above-target inflation implies higher-for-longer rates, suppressing bond issuance but boosting demand for inflation-linked analytics and commodity data (Platts).
Tail risk scenario. >4% inflation would likely freeze credit issuance further and pressure SPGI Ratings transaction revenue.
Extreme tail risk. Would signal stagflationary environment with major credit market disruption.

Directly involves SPGI's core business. S&P already downgraded US in 2011. Another downgrade (likely by Moody's, which downgraded in 2025) validates credit rating agency relevance but invites regulatory scrutiny. Note: US was downgraded in 2025 (resolved Yes on related market).

macro_events.spgi_relevance: Rate cuts stimulate bond issuance (positive for SPGI Ratings transaction revenue). Rate trajectory is the single most important macro variable for SPGI's cyclical revenue component.

no_coverage.finding: No dedicated 'financial crisis' prediction market found. Closest proxies are recession markets and bank failure markets listed above.
no_coverage.note: Polymarket structures crisis risk through component markets (recession probability, bank failures, debt downgrades) rather than a single 'financial crisis' event.

no_coverage.finding: No prediction markets found for individual corporate credit rating changes. Only sovereign rating markets exist.
no_coverage.note: Corporate credit rating prediction markets would be highly relevant for SPGI but do not exist on current platforms.

synthesis.macro_backdrop_for_spgi: Prediction markets paint a moderately stressed macro environment for SPGI: 76% chance inflation stays above 3% (negative for bond issuance volume), 28.5% recession risk (mixed — reduces issuance but boosts risk analytics demand), and 28.5% chance of another US sovereign downgrade (directly involves SPGI's peer group). The implied probability distribution suggests the market consensus is for 'stagflation-lite' — persistent inflation without outright recession — which historically compresses SPGI Ratings transaction revenue while supporting subscription-based Market Intelligence revenue.
key_risks: 76% probability of >3% inflation implies higher-for-longer rates, suppressing bond issuance (SPGI Ratings transaction revenue at risk)
28.5% recession probability — if realized, could reduce SPGI revenue growth by 5-10% based on 2008-2009 precedent
28.5% chance of another US sovereign downgrade — regulatory/reputational risk for rating agencies
SPGI missed Q4 2025 earnings consensus — potential negative momentum signal
key_tailwinds: Macro uncertainty drives demand for SPGI Market Intelligence subscriptions and risk analytics
Sovereign downgrades and credit stress increase ratings surveillance activity
If Fed cuts rates (Kalshi markets track this), bond issuance would rebound sharply — positive for SPGI Ratings
